summary: A circa-1936 steel lookout of about 100 feet near Bamberg; the register says it is now privately owned and still hosts Forestry Commission radio equipment.

facts.design: Steel tower, possibly Bethlehem Steel (per register), with a 7 x 7 x 10 ft steel cab

access.note: Tower and ground residence are now privately owned, per the register.

evidence.supports: built circa 1936; register says it appears to be a Bethlehem Steel tower
evidence.quote: This 100-foot tower was built circa 1936 and appears to be a Bethlehem Steel tower.

evidence.supports: 100-foot steel tower with 7 x 7 ft cab
evidence.quote: A 100-foot steel tower with a 7' x 7' cab.

evidence.supports: Eastern US Lookouts lists the SC Forestry Commission
evidence.quote: South Carolina - Bamberg County - South Carolina Forestry Commission

evidence.supports: tower and ground residence now privately owned
evidence.quote: The tower and ground residence are now privately owned.

evidence.supports: keeper's house nearby, original Forestry Commission sign, and radio repeater equipment on the tower
evidence.quote: The keeper's house is located nearby, along with an original SC Forestry Commission sign, and the tower still appears to host SCFC radio repeater equipment.

evidence.supports: original location and fair to good condition
evidence.quote: Still located in its original location, it looks to be in fair to good condition.

corrections.why: The register says the tower and ground residence are now privately owned.

notes_for_editor: Ownership and agency conflict, not resolved: the record says state ownership, the register says a private owner, and the Eastern US Lookouts page lists the SC Forestry Commission. The register also mentions an original Forestry Commission sign and Forestry Commission repeater equipment. Circa 1936 and Bethlehem Steel are the register's own tentative wording. Two web searches found no newspaper or Forestry Commission record of this tower.
